name: GPT-5.6 Sol
description: Flagship tier of the GPT-5.6 family (July 9, 2026). Scores 94.6% on GPQA Diamond, 90.4% on BrowseComp and 89% on FrontierMath Tier 1-3. 922K input / 128K output; requests above 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output.

name: GPT-5.6 Terra
description: Balanced tier of the GPT-5.6 family: most of Sol's capability at 40% of the price. OpenAI cut Terra pricing 20% on July 30, 2026. The default choice for production workloads that don't need frontier reasoning.

name: GPT-5.6 Luna
description: Fastest and cheapest GPT-5.6 tier, cut 80% in price on July 30, 2026. At $0.20 per million input tokens it is priced for high-volume classification, routing and extraction rather than deep reasoning.

name: Claude Sonnet 5
description: Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet yet (June 30, 2026), approaching Opus 4.8 quality at a fraction of the cost. Best for agentic coding, multi-file refactors, long-document analysis and computer use. Introductory pricing of $2/$10 runs through August 31, 2026.

name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
description: Google's speed-and-value play against GPT-5.6 (July 21, 2026). 1M-token context, knowledge cutoff March 2026, and the strongest price-per-task ratio in the current flagship group for high-throughput work.

name: Kimi K3
description: The first open-weight model in the ~3T parameter class (July 16, 2026): a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts with native vision and a 1M-token context. Cached input drops to $0.30 per million, which makes repeated long-context work unusually cheap.

name: GPT-4o
description: OpenAI's flagship multimodal model with native text, vision, and audio capabilities, offering strong all-around performance.

name: GPT-4o Mini
description: Cost-efficient small model replacing GPT-3.5 Turbo, offering strong performance at a fraction of GPT-4o's cost.

name: o1
description: OpenAI's first reasoning model that uses chain-of-thought to solve complex math, science, and coding problems.

name: o3
description: Advanced reasoning model succeeding o1, with significantly improved math and coding performance at reduced pricing.

name: o3-mini
description: Cost-efficient reasoning model with adjustable effort levels (low/medium/high), matching o1 at medium on STEM tasks.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Oct 2024)
description: Updated Sonnet with computer use capability and improved coding (93.7% HumanEval), the most popular coding model of late 2024.

name: Claude 3 Opus
description: Anthropic's original flagship model, excelling at complex analysis and nuanced writing with strong safety alignment.

name: Claude 3 Haiku
description: Anthropic's fastest and most affordable model, designed for near-instant responses on simple queries and classification.

name: Claude Opus 4
description: Anthropic's first Opus 4 generation model with extended thinking capabilities and strong agentic coding performance.

name: Claude Sonnet 4
description: Balanced mid-tier model in the Claude 4 generation, offering strong coding and reasoning at competitive pricing.

name: Claude Opus 4.5
description: Major upgrade with 87% GPQA and 80.9% SWE-bench, the highest-rated Anthropic model before the 4.6 generation.

name: Claude Opus 4.6
description: Current #1 on Chatbot Arena (1496 ELO), with 99.8% AIME 2025 and 80.8% SWE-bench, leading in coding and hard prompts.

name: Claude Opus 4.7
description: Anthropic's most capable generally available model, launched in April 2026 with stronger long-horizon agentic performance and the same $5/$25 MTok pricing as Opus 4.6.

name: Claude Opus 4.8
description: Anthropic's May 2026 Opus upgrade. 4x less likely to overlook code flaws than Opus 4.7. First model to complete every case on Super-Agent benchmark. Highest score ever on Legal Agent Benchmark at launch. Fast mode available at $10/$50 per million tokens.

name: Claude Opus 5
description: Anthropic's July 2026 Opus release. Stronger than Opus 4.8 on coding, knowledge work, long-horizon agentic tasks, and cost per completed task. Same $5/$25 per million token base pricing, with Fast mode available.

name: Claude Fable 5
description: Anthropic's first generally available Mythos-class model (June 9, 2026), restored globally after the June access pause. Built for long-horizon autonomous work, advanced coding, vision, memory, and professional tasks. Priced at $10/$50 per million tokens, with safety routing for high-risk requests.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
description: Latest Sonnet with adaptive reasoning, 89.9% GPQA and 79.6% SWE-bench, excellent balance of speed and intelligence.

name: Claude Haiku 4.5
description: Anthropic's fastest model in the 4.5 generation, offering near-Sonnet quality at Haiku-tier speed and pricing.

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
description: Google's first million-token context model (up to 2M), excelling at long-document understanding and multimodal tasks.

name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
description: Ultra-fast and affordable multimodal model with native tool use, image/audio generation, and 1M token context.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
description: Google's hybrid thinking model combining fast responses with deep reasoning, top performer on coding and math benchmarks.

name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
description: Fast reasoning model with excellent cost efficiency, balancing speed and intelligence for high-throughput applications.

name: Gemini 3 Pro
description: Google's late-2025 Pro model with 94.3% GPQA and 100% AIME 2025, a 1M context window, and strong multimodal reasoning for complex workflows.

name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
description: Google's newer Pro generation surfaced at Cloud Next 2026 as its most capable model for complex workflows, with 1M context and Gemini 3-class multimodal support.

name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
description: Ultra-low latency model designed for sub-second responses at scale. Google's cheapest frontier-adjacent model.

name: Llama 3.1 405B
description: Largest open-source model at release, competitive with GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet across most benchmarks.

name: Llama 3.1 70B
description: Strong mid-size open-source model offering excellent performance-to-cost ratio for self-hosted deployments.

name: Llama 3.1 8B
description: Compact open-source model suitable for on-device and edge deployments with surprisingly strong capabilities for its size.

name: Llama 4 Scout
description: Open-weight, natively multimodal Llama 4 model designed for efficient deployment and long-context workloads.

name: Llama 4 Maverick
description: Higher-capability open-weight Llama 4 model in Meta's multimodal MoE generation, available for download via llama.com.

name: Mistral Large 2
description: Mistral's flagship with 123B parameters, multilingual in 80+ languages, and strong code generation (92% HumanEval).

name: Mistral Large 3
description: Open-weight Apache 2.0 MoE flagship from Mistral 3 generation with strong multilingual and multimodal performance.

name: DeepSeek V3
description: Chinese open-source MoE model rivaling GPT-4o at a fraction of the cost, trained for under $6M causing industry shock.

name: DeepSeek R1
description: Open-source reasoning model matching o1 performance with 97.3% MATH-500, disrupted the AI industry with its efficiency.

name: DeepSeek V3.2
description: Updated open-source model with near-frontier capability at 1/20th the cost of GPT-5.5.

name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
description: DeepSeek's April 2026 V4-generation API model focused on speed and lower-cost production inference.

name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
description: DeepSeek's higher-capability V4-generation API model introduced in April 2026 for deeper reasoning and agentic workloads.

name: Grok-2
description: xAI's second-gen model with real-time X/Twitter data access, competitive with GPT-4o on standard benchmarks.

name: Grok-3
description: Trained on xAI's Colossus supercluster, top-tier math reasoning with 93.3% AIME 2025 score.

name: Grok 4.3
description: xAI's newer flagship family with top-ranked LMArena results for both thinking and non-thinking modes.

name: Grok 4.20
description: xAI's latest model with improved reasoning and coding capabilities.

name: Qwen 2.5 72B Instruct
description: Alibaba's leading open-source model with strong multilingual and coding capabilities, competitive with Llama 3.1 70B.

name: GPT-4.5 Preview
description: OpenAI's largest and most knowledgeable non-reasoning model with broad world knowledge and reduced hallucinations.

name: GPT-5.2
description: OpenAI's current-gen flagship with 400K context, 92.4% GPQA and 100% AIME 2025, strong reasoning at reduced cost.

name: GPT-5.4
description: OpenAI's March 2026 frontier model for professional reasoning and agentic coding, released across ChatGPT, API, and Codex.

name: GPT-5.4 Mini
description: Faster and lower-cost GPT-5.4 variant for high-volume coding, subagents, and computer-use workloads.

name: GPT-5.4 Nano
description: OpenAI's smallest GPT-5.4-class model, optimized for ultra-cheap classification, extraction, and lightweight agent sub-tasks.

name: GPT-5.5
description: OpenAI's April 2026 flagship model for real-world coding and professional workflows, with stronger agentic performance and a 1M API context window.

name: GPT-5.5 Pro
description: OpenAI's most capable model as of May 2026. Leads the Arena leaderboard. 52.5% fewer hallucinations than GPT-5.4. Enhanced personalization with conversation memory and Gmail integration.

name: GPT-5.5 Instant
description: Fast default model powering ChatGPT for all users. Optimized for speed while maintaining GPT-5.5 quality.

name: Kimi K2.5
description: Chinese model with the highest HumanEval score ever recorded (99.0%), excelling at code generation and reasoning.

name: Kimi K2.6
description: Moonshot AI's latest model with strong multilingual and long-context capabilities. $20B valuation.

name: GLM 5.1
description: Chinese frontier model from Zhipu AI. Competitive with Claude Sonnet at a fraction of the cost.

name: GLM 5
description: Previous generation Zhipu model, still competitive with Western mid-tier models.

name: Qwen3.8 Max
description: Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts, launched 3 August 2026 and released with open weights. Takes text, images and video, answers up to 128K tokens at a time, and cached input drops to $0.25 per million. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Grok 4.6
description: xAI's August 2026 flagship, built for long-running agents and coding. Watch the billing cliff: once a prompt reaches 200K tokens the whole request is charged at $4.00 input and $12.00 output per million, not just the tokens above the line. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Seed 2.1 Turbo
description: ByteDance's cheap production workhorse, released in August 2026. Output length matches the context window, so it can write as much as it reads. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
description: Google's August 2026 Flash model with a 1M-token context and 64K output. The listed price is introductory and runs to 31 December 2026, after which it doubles to $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
description: Google's third Flash release in six weeks, shipped 2 September 2026 — a better model at the same price as 3.7 Flash, with a 1M-token context and 64K output. The $0.75 input / $3.75 output rate is introductory and doubles to $1.50 / $7.50 on 1 January 2027. Prices checked 3 September 2026.

name: Muse Spark 1.3
description: Meta's reasoning model, released early September 2026 and delivered through Muse Code and the Meta Model API. A 1M-token context with text, image, and video input; it lands around #6 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The standard endpoint is $1.25 input / $4.25 output per million (cached input $0.15); a contributor tier runs $0.10 / $0.20 if Meta may train on your prompts, and a higher 'max reasoning' tier is in limited preview. Prices checked 3 September 2026.

name: GLM 5.3
description: Z.ai's coding and cyber-defence model, released 14 August 2026. It reuses the GLM 5.2 base unchanged and takes its reported gains from post-training alone. Open weights were promised about two weeks after launch and had not appeared as of 1 September 2026. Cached input $0.26 per million. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Qwen3.8 27B
description: A 27-billion-parameter dense multimodal model under Apache 2.0, released 14 August 2026. Small enough to run yourself, takes text, images and video, and stretches from 262K to 1M tokens of context. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: GLM 5.3 Flash
description: Open weights under MIT, released 26 August 2026, with a 1M-token context at fifteen cents per million input. A launch promotion halved input to $0.075 until 9 September 2026. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Qwen3.8 Flash
description: Released the same day as GLM 5.3 Flash, 26 August 2026, at almost the same price. Native context is 262K tokens and extends to 1M with YaRN. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: GLM 5.2
description: The open-weight Chinese model that made the case that a frontier-class base need not be expensive, released 16 June 2026 with a 1M-token context. Still the base underneath GLM 5.3. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Claude Fable 5.1
description: Anthropic's flagship, released 1 September 2026. Input and output prices are unchanged from Fable 5, but cache reads fall from $1.00 to $0.25 per million, a 75% cut that makes repeated long-context work far cheaper than the headline price suggests. Cache writes $12.50 for five minutes, $20.00 for an hour. 1M-token context, up to 128K tokens per answer. Prices checked 1 September 2026.

name: Claude Mythos 5.1
description: The same model as Fable 5.1 without the production safeguards, released the same day and priced identically. Not generally available: access runs through restricted programmes for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organisations that need capabilities those safeguards normally constrain. Prices checked 1 September 2026.
